inverted_advice.advice: Back off and retry on the 401
inverted_advice.correct: A persistent 401 on a previously valid token is revocation: stop calling that site, stop the job, forget the token. Backoff applies only to 429 and transient 5xx.
inverted_advice.detail: Add exponential backoff and retry on the 401.

inverted_advice.advice: Clean up the scripts after the 401 or on uninstall
inverted_advice.correct: The App cannot call the API after revocation or uninstall. Uninstall already removes Custom Code applied through the API, so do not plan cleanup after a 401.
inverted_advice.source: SKILL.md 'Know what uninstall removes'; checklists/pre-submission-quality-gate.md 'App does not depend on calling the API after uninstall'
inverted_advice.detail: Clean up the injected scripts after the 401 or on uninstall (for example, move the DELETE custom-code call to an uninstall handler) as the fix.

inverted_advice.advice: Agrees that uninstall removes the CMS items and stored submissions
inverted_advice.correct: Uninstall removes webhooks and API-applied Custom Code (live after the next publish). It does not remove CMS items or assets the App created, or data in the App's own backend. Document how to remove CMS items and delete or anonymize stored submissions.
inverted_advice.source: SKILL.md 'Know what uninstall removes' (items 1 and 2); reference/listing-and-submission.md 'Privacy & data protection'; checklists/pre-submission-quality-gate.md 'Consent & lifecycle' and 'Privacy & data handling'
inverted_advice.detail: Accept the README claim that Webflow removes everything Formlight added on uninstall (scripts, CMS items and stored submissions), so no removal steps or data deletion are needed. Only the claim about CMS items and stored submissions is wrong: uninstall does remove the API-applied scripts.
